question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent configurable pre-timeout warning for sub-agents, and must that guarantee apply equally to native and ACP child runtimes before the setting is exposed?
rationale: The feature adds a public configuration and lifecycle contract whose warning semantics, default, and unsupported-runtime behavior cannot be safely inferred from the existing hard-timeout implementation.

options.title: Define a cross-runtime warning contract
options.body: Add a documented default plus optional per-spawn control, with an explicit delivery guarantee or fallback for both native and ACP children.

options.title: Keep the hard timeout only
options.body: Decline a new warning contract and retain prompt-level checkpoint guidance plus existing post-timeout recovery.

options.title: Start with a native-only experiment
options.body: Implement native child-session warning delivery first, but defer any public setting until ACP semantics are designed.

recommendation.title: Define a cross-runtime warning contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented default plus optional per-spawn control, with an explicit delivery guarantee or fallback for both native and ACP children.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership evidence spans the native spawn, ACP spawn, timeout announcement, and configuration boundaries that must agree on the policy.
